name: Contempora Fabrics Inc
old_description: Founded in 1972, Contempora Fabrics is an employee owned circular knit company based in Lumberton, NC.  Starting as a contract knitter, Contempora has evolved into one of the premier knit fabric manufacturers in the US.  With over 200 machines and a capacity of 2 million pounds per month, Contempora has continued to expand to meet the needs of our customers.
about:
Contempora Fabrics, founded in 1972 by Lacy C. Nance, is an employee-owned circular knit manufacturer based in Lumberton, North Carolina. The company began as a contract knitter producing fine gauge interlock and single knit fabrics, and transitioned to full employee ownership through an ESOP in 1988.

Today the company operates 175 circular knitting machines in a 150,000-square-foot facility on 29 acres, with a monthly capacity of 2 million pounds of fabric. It offers both greige and finished fabrics, supported by an in-house research and development team that provides fabric analysis and works with the latest fiber technologies. The lint-controlled, humidity-defined manufacturing environment allows simultaneous processing of all fiber types.

Contempora serves brands, retailers, and manufacturers across performance and activewear, athletic and team apparel, fashion and formal wear, casual and career wear, intimate apparel and shapewear, and swimwear and beachwear. Its client base includes companies such as Boombah, and the staff has extensive experience handling USMCA and CAFTA-DR shipping requirements for weekly container shipments to Central America.

The company emphasizes its ESOP culture as a driver of quality and on-time delivery, alongside sustainability initiatives that have reduced energy consumption through lighting upgrades and recycling of byproducts such as cardboard tubes, scrap yarn, and plastic. Competitive pricing and short lead times are cited as daily commitments.

about:
Cope Plastics Inc operates a fabrication and distribution branch in Fargo, North Dakota, supported by its headquarters in Alton, Illinois. The Fargo facility sits about four miles from Hector International Airport and serves as a regional hub for custom plastic fabrication and material supply.

The branch runs advanced CNC equipment — saws, routers, and drills — to produce custom plastic parts, prototypes, and cut-to-size components. Its 7,000-square-foot warehouse stocks a range of engineering plastics including sheets, rods, and tubes in materials such as ACM, acrylic, HDPE, nylon, polycarbonate, polyurethane, and UHMW. The company also fabricates specialized components like pistons, thrust washers, rollers, bushings, and boom pads for industrial equipment.

Cope Plastics serves industries including fluid handling, food and beverage, construction, mining operations, material handling, and safety and security. Customers range from food-processing plants needing lubricant-free rollers to mining operations using nylon sheaves for forklifts and crane boom pads. The company also supplies conduit duct spacers, ground protection mats, and outrigger pads for construction and utility applications.

The company emphasizes a streamlined manufacturing process and rigorous quality control to minimize lead times, distinguishing itself from standard plastic distributors by offering USA-made fabricated parts alongside stocked materials. Local delivery is available on qualifying orders.

name: Copper Star Home Medical Supplies
old_description: Copper Star Home Medical has been Phoenix’s locally trusted home medical equipment store for over 22 years. With the largest medical supply showroom in Arizona, if you need it, there’s a good chance we have it. Whether you’re recovering from surgery, managing a chronic condition, or looking for equipment that makes daily life safer and more comfortable at home, our Phoenix store has what you need. That includes power lift chairs, home hospital beds, manual and power wheelchairs, mobility scooters, walkers and rollators, CPAP and BiPAP machines, portable and home oxygen concentrators, knee scooters, patient lifts, bath and shower safety equipment, compression garments, orthopedic bracing, and aids to daily living.
about:
Copper Star Home Medical Supplies operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where it has served the metropolitan area for over 22 years. The company runs what it describes as the largest medical supply showroom in the state, with additional locations in Tempe, Mesa, and Surprise. Ownership structure and founding individuals are not publicly disclosed.

The retailer stocks a broad range of durable medical equipment for sale or weekly and monthly rental. Inventory includes power lift chairs, hospital beds, manual and power wheelchairs, mobility scooters, walkers, rollators, CPAP and BiPAP machines, portable and stationary oxygen concentrators, knee scooters, patient lifts, bath safety equipment, compression garments, orthopedic bracing, and daily living aids. All showroom units are fully assembled for hands‑on evaluation before purchase or rental.

Customers include patients recovering from surgery, individuals managing chronic conditions, seasonal “snowbird” residents, and caregivers. The company works directly with Medicare, Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Arizona, Devoted Health, Homelink, Integrated Home Care Services, One Call, and Prospect Medical Group, and accepts FSA and HSA payments. Healthcare professionals also refer patients for equipment fitting and procurement.

Copper Star emphasizes a consultative approach: staff help clients decide between renting and buying, navigate insurance coverage, and select equipment suited to Arizona’s climate and the needs of an aging population. Its Bell Road location sits near HonorHealth Deer Valley Medical Center and Mayo Clinic Hospital, supporting post‑discharge transitions.

about:
Copper Wolf Custom Fabrication operates from Golden, Colorado, in the foothills of the Rocky Mountains. The business traces its inception to 2014, when Chris “CL” Long and Rebecca Long met in welding school and later turned their shared trade into a company. The couple, who had previously run a fabrication shop together, formally launched their own venture in 2018.

The shop produces custom metalwork for both residential and commercial clients. Its portfolio includes handmade furnishings, decorative pieces, garden gates, handrails, stair systems, and structural railings. Every item is fabricated to order using 100 % American‑grade steel and reclaimed lumber, then finished with an indoor/outdoor‑rated powder coat. The facility handles welding, forming, and coating in‑house, though the company does not disclose its square footage or headcount.

Customers range from homeowners seeking one‑of‑a‑kind interior and exterior accents to businesses needing custom architectural metalwork. The company cites projects for private homes and commercial spaces alike, and it holds a membership in the Golden Chamber of Commerce.

The founders emphasize material provenance and finish durability as their differentiators: domestic steel, recycled wood, and a powder‑coat system rated for harsh outdoor exposure. They position the shop as a source for bespoke, American‑made metal pieces rather than volume production.

name: Corbitt Manufacturing Company
old_description: Since 1948 we have supported the transportation, construction, industrial tool, farm and foodservice industries. We deliver the top-quality products you need, when and where you need it. Guaranteed.
about:
Corbitt Manufacturing Company operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility in Paragould, Arkansas. Founded in 1948, the business began as a diversified contract manufacturer specializing in permanent-mold aluminum castings, machined components, custom tooling, and complete assemblies. In 2019, the company was acquired by The Greenbrier Companies and now operates as a Greenbrier subsidiary.

The plant houses three CNC machining centers and three furnaces feeding multiple pour lines, supported by grinders, broaching machines, milling machines, lathes, and a range of presses including a Dake 375-ton hydraulic press, a Bliss SC2 500-ton press, and a Niagara HBM 175-ton press. Standard permanent-mold castings run up to 75 pounds with a maximum mold envelope of 48 by 62 inches, while machining services cover prototype design, reverse engineering, wire and RAM EDM, gear cutting, jig and fixture building, and assembly. Production volumes span from one-off prototypes to several hundred thousand units annually.

Corbitt serves OEMs in earth-moving, mining, agricultural, electrical, transportation, recreation, and food-service markets. In transportation it produces dock cleats, transmission casings, manifolds, and railroad-car parts as the industry shifts from iron to aluminum. For food service it re-engineered a motor housing that eliminated leakage and cut scrap rates. Electrical work includes explosion-proof receptacles and power-line connectors, while powertrain projects focus on light- and heavy-duty gearboxes held to super-close tolerances.

The company emphasizes a "what you need, when and where you need it" delivery guarantee backed by in-house testing protocols that fast-track part deployment. Engineering staff provide troubleshooting expertise on every project, positioning Corbitt as a problem-solving partner rather than a pure production shop.

name: Corporate Casuals
old_description: The climbers, skiers, and backcountry wanderers at Marmot surprise people each day since 1971.
about:
Corporate Casuals operates from Concord, Massachusetts, where it has been decorating apparel since 1980. The company began as an embroidery studio and, after four years, replaced its original equipment with the production facility it runs today. Ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The shop specializes in custom embroidery and printing on a wide range of garments and accessories—polo shirts, jackets, fleece, hats, bags, and scrubs—using state-of-the-art embroidery machines and digital printing technology. With a staff of about 15, the facility has decorated well over eight million items to date and is set up for on-demand, single-unit production with no minimum order requirements.

Customers include small businesses, corporate teams, non-profits, healthcare providers ordering scrubs and lab coats, and sports organizations needing activewear. Corporate Casuals sources blank apparel from national warehouses and decorates premium brands such as The North Face, Carhartt, Nike, Under Armour, Marmot, and New Era.

The company emphasizes personal service from industry professionals, free setup on studio designs, and what it describes as the fastest standard processing time in the industry. Its model was built to make single-unit orders profitable, allowing clients to order exactly what they need without inventory risk.

name: Cosco Air Conditioning & Refrigeration
old_description: Cosco has been providing the supplies and materials Hawaii's AC contractors have needed for 58 years. Visit one of our locations today to see how we can help you.
about:
Cosco Air Conditioning & Refrigeration has served Hawaii’s HVAC contractors from its base in Kailua-Kona since 1961. The family‑owned company was founded to supply the materials and equipment that local air‑conditioning and refrigeration professionals needed, and it has remained under family operation for over six decades.

The business operates a specialty division, Cosco Custom Coils, which manufactures direct‑fit HVAC coils and OEM replacements. The division converts microchannel designs to tube‑and‑fin configurations and produces condenser, evaporator, and chilled‑water coils using copper tube and fin options. In addition to coil fabrication, the company provides machining and metalworking services and applies specialty paints, coatings, and additives. Cosco also acts as the state’s largest Daikin dealer, distributing mini‑split systems and other equipment. The operation employs roughly 50 people.

Primary customers are HVAC contractors across Hawaii, along with commercial and industrial facilities that require heat‑ and energy‑recovery ventilators. The company’s product range covers replacement parts and accessories for air conditioners, refrigeration hardware, and ventilation equipment.

Cosco emphasizes its long‑standing local presence and the ability to deliver custom coil solutions on short notice, a capability developed to address the specific climate and installation challenges of the Hawaiian market.

name: Council Stainless & Sheet Metal
old_description: Custom items for commercial kitchen equipment, specialty enclosures, signage and more.
about:
Council Stainless & Sheet Metal has operated from Oklahoma City, Oklahoma since 1979. The custom metal fabrication company provides design, fabrication, and field installation services for a range of industries. No founders or ownership details are disclosed.

The 6,000-square-foot shop houses a 220-ton press brake and supports CNC sheet metal fabrication, CNC cold forming, waterjet cutting, and CAD design. The company works with stainless steel, copper, carbon steel, aluminum, and other specialty metals to produce commercial kitchen equipment, restaurant tables, exhaust vent hoods, sinks, countertops, cabinets, enclosures, racks, fascia systems, sign components, and complete assemblies. It handles both individual parts and sub-assemblies.

Customers span commercial food service, architectural metalwork, oilfield equipment, and general industrial assemblies. The firm serves contractors, OEMs, and end users needing custom stainless steel and sheet metal components, including residential vent hoods and signage.

The company emphasizes a single-source model: design, fabrication, and field installation under one roof. It also offers repair and maintenance services for sheet metal items originally fabricated by others.
